 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO i) ISSUE A WRIT IN THE NATURE OF CERTIORARI QUASHING THE GENERAL AWARD BEARING NO.KIADB/BHUSWA-2/ANH/MF DATED:04/05/2019, PASSED BY THE THIRD RESPONDENT VIDE ANNEXURE-A AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The present petition is filed by the petitioner seeking writ of certiorari to quash the general award passed by respondent No.3 on 04.05.2019 in respect of property bearing Survey No.49/2 measuring 1 acre 14 guntas of land situated at Adinarayana Hosahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapur Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District and for a further direction to the respondents to consider the NC:
2023:KHC:32714 case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act.

2. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that though as on the date the general award was passed there was no pending litigation or there was any impediment for the respondents to pass the consent award as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, the Respondent No.3 proceeded to pass the general award and that in view of the law laid down in Smt. Ningamma Vs The State of Karnataka & others [W.P.No.6198/2015 D.D. 25.8.2015] passing of the consent award under Section 29(2) is not only beneficial but would also put an end to the challenge to the award.

sentences.text: Hence, he submits that the general award in the circumstances be set aside and the respondents be directed to pass the consent award.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner drawing attention of this Court to order dated 05.06.2023 passed in W.P.No.9352/2023 in an identical matter submits similar order be passed in the instant case as Sri. sentences.text: Sri.B.B.Patil, learned counsel for respondents 2 and 3 submits that since petitioner did not approach KIADB, general award was passed and amount has been deposited before the Civil Court.

Learned counsel submits given some time respondents 2 and 3 would consider the case of the petitioner under Section 29(2) of the Act.
5.
Heard.
Perused the records.

6. Under identical circumstances, this Court in its order dated 05.06.2023 passed in W.P.9352/2023 while allowing the writ petition, has issued following directions:
"(i) The respondent Special Land Acquisition Officer of the KIADB is directed to consider the request of the petitioner for availing compensation by way of an agreement under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act and pass necessary orders within a period of three months from the date of release of this order.
(ii) The respondent - Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, is at liberty to withdraw the amount that has been deposited by it pursuant to the general award before the jurisdictional Court.

(iii) Needless to state that in the event of any dispute, the general award would stand restored."
NC: 2023:KHC:32714 In that view of the matter, petitioner is also entitled to the benefit of similar order.

Hence the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.

ii) The general award dated 04.05.2019 as per Annexure-A insofar as it relates to the extent of the petitioner's land is hereby set aside.
iii) The respondents are directed to consider the case of the petitioner in terms of the order/directions extracted herein above within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
Sd/-
